text: The ovens were humming their low steady hum. It was Thursday, 3:17 AM. He wiped flour from his forearms. He walked to the front counter. It was just as it had been for the past six weeks. On the glass display case sat a single worn paperback. It was The Shadow of the Wind. He picked it up, feeling its familiar weight, its dog-eared pages. It was slightly warmer than the air in the shop. Usually he would have put it in the bin, thinking a confused customer had mistaken the bakery's drop-box slot for a library return. But tonight, something felt different. He opened the book to the bookmarked page. A square of notebook paper slipped out and fluttered to the counter. He unfolded it. The handwriting was jagged, hurried. The note said, "I know you're reading it. Keep going. Page 204 changes everything." His heart hammered against his ribs. Sharp sudden rhythm against the quiet hum of the mixers. The shop was empty. Shadows stretched long across the tiled floor. He looked back at the note, then the book. With trembling fingers, he turned to page 204. The text blurred before his eyes. He closed the book, pressed it flat against the counter, and reached for his pen.
